---
title: "Quickstart"
---

Write your first hook in under five minutes. By the end, Claude Code stops your agent from
finishing a UI change it never looked at, and you have a second hook that proves itself with a
passing test.

Every command runs through `uvx`, so nothing is installed.

## 1. Scaffold

```bash
uvx capt-hook init
```

`init` creates `.claude/hooks/`, wires Claude Code's settings, and installs the two helper
skills. You're already live, so there's no separate wiring step.

## 2. Read your first hook

`init` dropped an example into `.claude/hooks/`. At its core is one declarative value built from
an action and two conditions.

<!-- gd-embed-fragment: canonical_hook -->

The action is `gate(...)`, which blocks the agent at `Stop` with the message you give it. The
`only_if` condition makes the gate fire only when the agent edited a file matching one of these
globs, while `skip_if` keeps the gate quiet if the agent already used `agent-browser` this
session. That's the whole model. An event, conditions that decide when it fires, and an action.

## 3. Watch it fire

Reload the project so Claude Code picks up the settings. Edit a file under `src/components/` and
try to end the turn. The gate blocks with your message until the agent reviews the change with
`agent-browser`.

## 4. Test your hooks

No git-hook tool can do this part, where every deterministic hook carries its own tests. Add a
second hook to `.claude/hooks/safety.py`:

```python
from captain_hook import Allow, Block, Input, block_command

block_command(
    ["git", "stash"],
    reason="Use jj instead",
    hint="Run `jj shelve`",
    tests={
        Input(command="git stash"): Block(),    # this command is blocked
        Input(command="git status"): Allow(),   # this one is fine
    },
)
```

Run the tests from your project root, where `--hooks` defaults to `.claude/hooks`:

```bash
uvx capt-hook test
```

```
.claude/hooks/safety.py
  PASS  Input(command='git stash')    expected Block, got Block
  PASS  Input(command='git status')   expected Allow, got Allow

2 passed, 0 failed
```

Break an expectation and the line flips to `FAIL` and the command exits non-zero. Drop the same
check into CI and a regressed hook fails the build. LLM- and signal-based hooks can't run without
a live model, so they report `SKIP` instead of failing.
